entry.title: Object of the Sun's Desire
entry.summary: Today would have been Elisa's 70th birthday. Since her passing in February, I have honored her in several concrete ways, such as holding a celebration of life for her at the end of September and purchasing a work of sculpture that we had been thinking to acquire for a special location in our house. In a similar vein, by working with a foundry here in Colorado I've had an earlier work of sculpture converted from plaster to bronze. Elisa had bought the plaster version a few years before we met from her good friend Stuart Feldman, a very fine figurative sculptor in the Philadelphia area. It's always bothered me that we had only a plaster version because that material is quite fragile, so I thought that having a bronze version made would be a great way to honor Elisa and her friendship with Stuart. Thankfully I was able to collaborate with Stuart throughout the various steps of the lost wax process, and the folks at Art Castings in Loveland, Colorado completed the job with great expertise. The work, entitled "Object of the Sun's Desire", is absolutely gorgeous and how has a prominent spot in the living room right off the foyer - a fitting welcome to the house and life that Elisa and I built together....

entry.title: Joyful, Meaningful, Beautiful
entry.summary: Following up on my post about Shige Oishi's concept of psychological richness, I've continued to reflect on the aims of life, which has led me to the following formulation: for myself at least, I aspire to live a life that is joyful, meaningful, and beautiful....

entry.title: A Portrait of the Philosopher as a Young Man
entry.summary: The other day I found a photo of me reading Hobbes' Leviathan at the foot of Rodin's Thinker outside Philosophy Hall on the campus of Columbia University circa 1986 (the photo was used in advertisements for Columbia's Summer School in the New York Times). This brought back memories of my university studies and my unorthodox attitude toward philosophy even back then....
